findings.description: Rest period between polling cycles
findings.expected: Engine sleeps/rests between cycles to avoid busy-loop

findings.description: Historical data storage interval

findings.title: PendingUpload(server_config_id=None) violates NOT NULL FK constraint
findings.description: When RajAPI /sync/ telemetry push fails, code queued PendingUpload(server_config_id=None). Column has NOT NULL FK constraint — silently throws IntegrityError, swallowed by bare except. No retry, no visible error.
findings.root_cause: Copied SPCB PendingUpload pattern but RajAPI pushes have no ServerConfig row — they belong to the heartbeat layer, not SPCB.
findings.fix: Removed both PendingUpload queuing blocks. RajAPI telemetry retried naturally on next 60s heartbeat. Log only.

findings.title: Duplicate remote command execution — commands could fire twice
findings.description: send_heartbeat() already receives commands in the RajAPI response body and executes them. _poll_remote_commands() independently polls /api/v1/commands/pending every 60s and executes the same commands. factory_reset or restart_polling could fire twice.
findings.root_cause: Legacy MQTT replacement not retired when heartbeat-based command delivery was introduced.
findings.fix: Deleted _poll_remote_commands() function and removed its call. Commands now flow exclusively through heartbeat response, executed once.

findings.title: Auth function skips CENTRAL_API_KEY — retries use wrong legacy key
findings.description: _load_rajapi_auth() checked RajAPIConfig.auth_token in DB then fell back to legacy RAJAPI_API_KEY. Never checked CENTRAL_API_KEY (the primary key from license verify). Retries for RajAPI payloads would auth-fail on correctly licensed installs.
findings.root_cause: Written before CENTRAL_API_KEY auth model was introduced, never updated.
findings.fix: Deleted _load_rajapi_auth(). Imported _load_rajapi_config() from rajapi_sync.py (checks CENTRAL_API_KEY first). retry_pending_uploads() now calls _load_rajapi_config(db).

findings.title: 4 competing auth knobs with inconsistent resolution order
findings.description: CENTRAL_API_KEY, GATEWAY_ID+DEVICE_SECRET, RAJAPI_API_KEY (legacy), RajAPIConfig.auth_token (DB). Resolution order differs across the three original RajAPI paths. A key valid for heartbeat may fail for telemetry push.
findings.root_cause: Auth model evolved across releases without a consolidation pass.
findings.fix: Deferred. Decision: CENTRAL_API_KEY primary, GATEWAY_ID+DEVICE_SECRET for fingerprinting. Kill RAJAPI_API_KEY and RajAPIConfig.auth_token in Q4 cleanup pass.

findings.title: Duplicate _get_or_create_param logic across two route modules
findings.description: Both sync.py and spcb_sync.py implement their own parameter upsert logic. Any fix or behavioural change must be applied in two places, and they can silently diverge.
findings.root_cause: No shared helper module for common DB operations on the central server.
findings.fix: Extracted _get_or_create_param to deps.py:21-49. Both sync endpoints now import shared helper. sync.py -19 lines, spcb_sync.py -27 lines.

findings.title: Quality hardcoded as 'good'/'bad' instead of CPCB codes U/O/E/N
findings.description: spcb_sync.py stored quality as the strings 'good' and 'bad'. The client side (UltrON) uses CPCB standard codes: U=Valid, O=Out-of-range, E=Comms-fail, N=Negative, etc. Cross-site quality queries on RajAPI produced inconsistent results — CPCB compliance reports were wrong.
findings.root_cause: SPCB endpoint written without reference to the CPCB DataQuality enum on the client.
findings.fix: quality="good"/"bad" → "U"/"O" (CPCB valid/operational codes) at spcb_sync.py:127.

findings.title: Unnecessary thin wrapper _find_site delegates directly to find_site_by_key
findings.description: _find_site() was a 5-line function that only called find_site_by_key() with no added logic. Adds a call frame and a name to track with no benefit.
findings.root_cause: Premature abstraction — probably copy-pasted from another module.
findings.fix: Removed _find_site() and 2 lazy imports. find_site_by_key() called directly at the one call site. -6 lines.

findings.title: In-memory rate-limit dict _login_attempts is unbounded — memory leak under attack
findings.description: Rate limiting used a defaultdict(list) keyed by IP. Under a sustained login attack from many IPs, the dict grew without bound. In production on a Pi with limited RAM this would OOM.
findings.root_cause: TTL sweep or max-entries cap was never added to the in-memory store.
findings.fix: Added attempts[-10:] slice cap after each append. ponytail comment names the upgrade path (TTL sweep or Redis). One line.

findings.title: Heartbeat monitor is O(sites × devices) — updates all rows every 60s regardless of change
findings.description: monitor_heartbeats_loop() iterated ALL sites and ALL devices every 60 seconds issuing an UPDATE per device even if nothing changed. At 1000 sites × 50 devices = 50,000 UPDATE statements per minute.
findings.root_cause: Naive full-scan with unconditional write. No delta check.
findings.fix: Added _prev_online: set[int] delta tracker. Loop now only issues UPDATEs when a site's online status actually changes tick-to-tick. Eliminates ~99% of writes at steady state.

findings.title: Inconsistent error logging between is_active and AMC checks
findings.description: site.is_active check silently returned without logging. AMC expiry check logged last_error. An inactive site left no trace; an AMC-expired site did. Operator debugging was asymmetric.
findings.root_cause: Two separate guard clauses written at different times with different error-reporting conventions.
findings.fix: Added logger.warning() to both is_active and amc_expiry guards with site ID and name.

findings.title: No DELETE endpoint for calibration jobs
findings.description: Calibration jobs could be created and approved but never deleted. No backend route or frontend button existed.
findings.root_cause: Feature gap — calibration job lifecycle only included create/approve/reject.
findings.fix: Added DELETE /calibration/{job_id} endpoint (calibration.py:276-288). Added red Delete button with confirm dialog in CalibrationScreen.tsx actions column.

findings.title: Calibration start error was generic — no actual error shown
findings.description: When /calibration/start failed, catch block showed 'Failed to start calibration job.' with no HTTP status or detail. User couldn't diagnose 401/404/422 errors.
findings.root_cause: catch block parsed nothing from the response.
findings.fix: Added res.json() parse on failure, passes body.detail or 'HTTP {status}' to toast message.

findings.title: DB Type exposed in Settings about section
findings.description: Settings/about info cards displayed 'DB Type: sqlite' — exposes backend technology choice to end users.
findings.root_cause: Information card included db_type key from backend response.
findings.fix: Removed DB Type row from the info cards array.

findings.title: Trend Data Table removed from Reports and Trends screens
findings.description: Both Reports and Trends screens had a redundant data table showing the same data already available in chart form. User requested removal.
findings.root_cause: Duplicate display of trend data — table added noise when chart covered the same data.
findings.fix: Removed the entire card section containing Trend Data Table from both screens.

findings.title: Offline device shows 0.00 in card and flat zero in charts
findings.description: WebSocket handler freezes last known value when device goes offline (AppContext.tsx:512). If last value was 0, ParameterCard showed '0.00' with offline styling. Historical data load converted null → 0 (DashboardScreen.tsx:353), making offline periods render as flat zero lines.
findings.root_cause: Multiple paths: (1) WS freeze preserves last value including 0, (2) null → 0 conversion in chart data load, (3) fill(0) for missing series, (4) Sparkline Math.min coerces null to 0.
findings.fix: ParameterCard shows 'Offline' text when status !== 'online'. DashboardScreen.tsx:353 → null instead of 0. DashboardScreen.tsx:355 → fill(null) instead of fill(0). Sparkline.tsx filters nulls before min/max, skips null in polyline, shows dashed line when all null.
